name: low stone proclamation platform set into a plaza floor, 3/4 top-down: large light flagstone top with a border of rim stones and an inlaid blue disc with a gold star, a one-course front riser and one step
label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_dais

surfaces.part: flagstone platform top with rim stones and inlaid blue disc

answer.evidence: The main body is a large flagstone top from rows 17 to 34, with a rim-stone border and a blue disc with a gold star inlaid at rows 20-27. A dark front-edge line at row 35 (#3e403d) ends the top. Below it, rows 36-37 are slightly darker (L=173, eave-shadow-like), then a vertical riser face runs through rows 38-45, with a dark outline at row 46. That gives a front face of about 11 rows under an 18-row top. The top is far deeper than a 1-2 row rim, so it reads as a 3/4 raised platform and not a flat slab. The step is not clearly separate from the riser. The grey strip at the right edge is too small to count as a receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's platform has about 3 lightness steps on the flagstone: a pale top, a mid grey for the mortar lines and a darker rim line. The stones are not shaded one by one like the reference paving, which has 7 visible tones with chiselled highlights and a dark mass. Measured facts: 4 visible tones per tile against 7 for paving and 3 for grass, and 7% near-flat coverage against 0% for both references. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline does carry a tint (a dark blue-grey around the platform), but it is applied uniformly around the whole shape, which reads as a sticker outline, not a dark material tone chosen selectively. The grass surround has only light speckle and large areas of near-uniform green, which is thinner than the reference grass clumps. The flagstone top and front riser are smooth, with only a few joint lines and no per-stone grain or speckle. The blue disc with the star is a good focal detail but small. Overall this is clean and readable, but shallower and flatter than the Beodeul paving.
